newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African vet says lions with AIDS pose no danger.
newsitem.headline: S.African vet says lions with AIDS pose no danger.

text.p: South Africa's chief vet reassured people on Wednesday that feline AIDS rife in lions in the country's biggest national park was no threat to humans -- or the animals themselves.

State veterinarian Dewald Keet also dismissed a widely held belief that the lions in the Kruger National Park had caught the disease by eating AIDS-infected refugees slipping across their terrain into South Africa.
"The virus has also been found in leopards but there has also been no effect on them and they are just as healthy as ever," Keet told the Star newspaper.
Feline AIDS affects 80 percent of the Kruger's hundreds of lions but seemed not to affect their population. It has been around in the park ecosystem for years, he said.
Some species are natural carriers of certain viruses that do not affect them. Buffalo carry foot and mouth disease without harm but it devastates domestic cattle.
Feline AIDS was identified in 1990 and has also been found in animals in European zoos. Keet said it could not be passed on to humans and had not come from them.
Park officials confirmed however that refugees from impoverished Mozambique did use the border park to try to sneak into richer South Africa, but not all made it.
"There have been attacks on people by buffalo, elephant, crocodiles and lions," a spokesman said. "Sometimes there are just bits of clothing left over."
